The grep search for `store.Memo` matched `store.MemoRelation` and `store.MemoShare` because they share the same prefix.

The word boundary filter already excluded `store.MemoRelation` and `store.MemoShare`. I also need to verify whether `fileserver` and `memo_service_comments.go` use `GetMemo`, since those functions accept `store.Memo` values even without explicit type names.

I am weighing the impact of the change: adding a field requires reviewing literal constructors and dialect scans, while removing or renaming a field breaks all field accesses. I will limit the list to actual type references, excluding indirect usage through GetMemo. I am now enumerating production files that directly mention `store.Memo`.

I have compiled the full list of production files that directly reference `store.Memo`. The list includes the struct definition in `store/memo.go`, the driver interface in `store/driver.go`, the SQLite, MySQL, and Postgres dialect implementations, and all API service files under `server/router/api/v1/` that touch memo operations.

I also found direct `store.Memo` references in SSE helpers, user notifications, RSS, email, and memopayload runner. The test files that reference the struct include SSE hub tests, memo service benchmarks and tests, user stats tests, frontend tests, RSS tests, and store-level memo, filter, relation, and migrator tests.

value.text: I am examining webhook.go to identify the exact request-signing mechanism.

Standard Webhooks uses HMAC-SHA256 with base64 headers: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, and webhook-signature (v1).

DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go; internal/webhook; Standard Webhooks (HMAC-SHA256)

q22.
DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go; internal/webhook; Standard Webhooks HMAC-SHA256

`CreateMemo` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` calls `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`, which loads the creator’s webhooks and posts via `webhook.PostAsync`. Delivery is `internal/webhook` (`Post` / `PostAsync` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`). When a signing secret is set, the request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 per Standard Webhooks (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`).

value.description: Inspect filter engine API and CEL usage

value.text: Checking helpers.go and render.go to confirm the filter parsing mechanism. Proto comments mention CEL.

The engine is CEL (Common Expression Language) via google/cel-go. It lives in internal/filter.

It compiles CEL to a dialect-agnostic condition tree. SQL per dialect is rendered via AppendConditions and CompileToStatement.

q25.
CEL Engine — internal/filter; CEL is compiled to a dialect-agnostic condition tree, then rendered to SQL via `AppendConditions`/`CompileToStatement` with `DialectSQLite`/`DialectMySQL`/`DialectPostgres`.

`ListMemosRequest.filter` is documented as a CEL expression in `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`. `internal/filter.Engine` (`internal/filter/engine.go`, cel-go) parses it; each dialect driver (e.g. `store/db/sqlite/memo.go`) calls `filter.AppendConditions` in `internal/filter/helpers.go` to append the rendered SQL fragment and args.

value.description: Check FK cascades and other DeleteMemo side tables

value.text:
Checking SQLite foreign key settings. Considering whether API DeleteMemo's comment deletions count as additional memo rows. Identifying which tables DeleteMemo directly affects or cascades to.

Directly affected: memo. Explicit cascade code covers memo_relation and attachment. Schema cascade covers memo_share. Reactions and inbox are unaffected. Checking sqlite.go for PRAGMA foreign key status.

SQLite disables foreign keys, so ON DELETE CASCADE on memo_share does not fire. MySQL and Postgres would trigger cascade deletions on that table.

Directly affected tables are `memo` and `attachment`. `memo_relation` is affected by explicit cascade code in `Store.DeleteMemo`. `memo_share` is affected by schema-level `ON DELETE CASCADE`, though it is not triggered by Go cleanup logic.

The API deletes comment memos first, but the affected tables remain unchanged. Reactions and inbox records are not deleted.

q26.
memo, memo_relation, attachment, memo_share

`Store.DeleteMemo` in `store/memo.go` deletes `memo_relation` rows (both directions) and linked `attachment` rows, then deletes the `memo` row. `memo_share` is removed by `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the MySQL/Postgres schemas (`store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql`). SQLite defines the same FK in `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` but opens with `foreign_keys(0)` in `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go`, so that cascade does not run there. Reactions and inbox rows are not deleted.

value.text:
The mechanism is `go:embed` of the compiled `dist/` directory combined with Echo static file serving and SPA fallback. It is wired in `frontend.go` and called from `server.go`.

The mechanism is an embedded filesystem created by `go:embed` of the `dist/` directory, served via Echo static file handling with SPA fallback. It is wired in `server/router/frontend/frontend.go` and attached to the Echo server in `server/server.go`.

The compiled React frontend is served via `go:embed` of the `dist` directory. Echo's static middleware serves the files. An SPA `index.html` fallback handles routing. This wiring lives in `server/router/frontend/frontend.go`, attached from `server/server.go`.

q27.
go:embed of `dist` + Echo static middleware with SPA `index.html` fallback; server/router/frontend/frontend.go

`//go:embed dist/*` embeds the built React assets. `FrontendService.Serve` mounts Echo `middleware.StaticWithConfig` and `spaFallbackMiddleware`. That is attached in production from `server/server.go` via `frontend.NewFrontendService(...).Serve(...)`.

value.description: Find frontend auth interceptor and backend validation

value.text: The frontend auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts` as `authInterceptor`. It manages two tokens: an access token sent as a Bearer header via in-memory `auth-state`, and a refresh token stored as an HttpOnly cookie with `credentials: include`. The backend package that validates these tokens is `server/auth` (specifically its `Authenticator` class).

The auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts` as `authInterceptor`. It manages two tokens: a Bearer JWT access token stored in localStorage via `auth-state`, and an HttpOnly refresh token sent via `credentials: include`.

The backend package that validates these tokens is `server/auth`.

q29.
web/src/connect.ts; access token (Bearer JWT) and refresh token (HttpOnly cookie); server/auth

`authInterceptor` in `web/src/connect.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` (from `web/src/auth-state.ts`) and uses `credentials: "include"` so the `memos_refresh` cookie is sent. On 401 it calls `AuthService.RefreshToken` and retries. The backend validates those tokens in `server/auth` (`Authenticator.AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2` / `AuthenticateByRefreshToken`); that package also accepts PATs, which the frontend interceptor does not issue.
